purpose: Corrects the cost column n+114(3) puts in front of the owner, and measures what the two routes would actually face.
population: The 33 non-acquired records among the 45 obtainable.
criterion: Landing domain of manifest.availableUrl, classified by an explicit per-domain table rather than a pattern.

evidence: parse_tei is called only from tests/test_fulltext.py
the available-pdf branch at fulltext.py:1001 records the URL and stops; manifest artifacts is []
missing: wire TEI into the manifest/artifact writer
pdfRouteWiring.correction: n+114(3) says the PDF route is "install a tool, no code needed". The parser is indeed already written and tested -- the hard part -- but acquisition and wiring are not. Both routes require code; the gap between them is smaller than install-versus-develop.

landingKindsNote: An HTML route sounds like 16 bespoke publisher layouts. Most of these are institutional repositories (DSpace/Pure/Eprints) with standard interfaces, plus figshare which has an API. That is a different cost shape from per-publisher scraping.
europePmcMissNote: Round 438 reported all 33 as miss and called the route exhausted. That conclusion stands, but miss conflates two causes: 32 have no PMCID at all, while 1 has a known PMCID whose fullTextXML returns 404 -- a 1995 article held in PMC as scans but outside the OA full-text subset. The remedies differ.
coverageStatement: Whether any of these repositories actually serves parseable full text is not tested here; that needs fetching, a capability this room does not enable on its own. The classification informs a cost estimate; it is not a promise of availability.
contentNote: Domains, counts and code locations only. No literature content.
